Scenario: Sign in with valid credentials and read the issued session
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/login with the demo credentials.
2. Inspect the Set-Cookie header.
3. GET /api/auth/session with the returned token.
ExpectedResult: 200 with a 64-character hex token, role ADMIN and expiresAt ≈ issuedAt + 8h; the cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax; the session endpoint returns the same actor.
ActualResult: 200, token length 64, cookie HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; TTL 8h; /api/auth/session returns the ADMIN actor.

Scenario: Session lifetime and expiry are reported by the API
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/login.
2. GET /api/auth/session.
ExpectedResult: 200 with user.role HR, sessionTtlHours 8 and expiresAt in the future.
ActualResult: sessionTtlHours = 8, expiresAt in the future, role HR.

Scenario: The page header shows the signed-in user and role badge
Steps:
1. Open /login and sign in.
2. Read the header next to the role badge.
ExpectedResult: role-badge shows ADMIN and current-user shows the full name “Amara Okafor”.
ActualResult: Header renders ADMIN · Amara Okafor (before the fix it rendered “undefined undefined” — see HR-BUG-007).
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-007.

Scenario: Wrong password is rejected without revealing whether the account exists
TestData: admin@example.com with a wrong password; ghost.user@example.com with the same password
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/login with a wrong password for an existing account.
2. POST /api/auth/login for an unknown account.
ExpectedResult: Both return 401 with the identical code INVALID_CREDENTIALS and the identical message.
ActualResult: Both responses were 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS with the same message; no account enumeration possible.

Scenario: Login payload validation returns 400 with field details
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/login without password.
2. POST /api/auth/login with a malformed email.
ExpectedResult: Both return 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with details[].path naming password / email.
ActualResult: 400 with details path "password" and, after the fix, 400 for the malformed email (was 401 — HR-BUG-003).
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-003.

Scenario: Signing out invalidates the server-side session
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/logout.
2. GET /api/auth/session with the same cookie/token.
ExpectedResult: 204 on logout, then 401 UNAUTHENTICATED on the session call.
ActualResult: 204 then 401 — the sessions row is deleted, not merely the cookie cleared.

Scenario: Boundary: five failed attempts lock the account for 15 minutes
TestData: employee7@example.com with 5 different wrong passwords, then the correct one
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/login with a wrong password five times.
2. POST /api/auth/login with the correct password.
ExpectedResult: The fifth failure (and any further attempt) returns 423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED; the correct password is still refused while the lock lasts.
ActualResult: After the fix: failure #5 returns 423 and the correct password also returns 423 with code ACCOUNT_LOCKED.
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-001 (lockout never triggered before the fix).

Scenario: Deep link survives the login redirect
TestData: GET /employees while signed out, then hr@example.com / Hr#1234567
Steps:
1. Open /employees (redirected to /login?next=%2Femployees).
2. Sign in as HR.
ExpectedResult: The browser lands on /employees and the list renders.
ActualResult: Redirects to /login?next=%2Femployees and, after the fix, continues to /employees after signing in.
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-005.

Scenario: Invalid credentials show an inline error and keep the typed email
Steps:
1. Open /login.
2. Fill the form with a wrong password and submit.
ExpectedResult: The page stays on /login, shows login-error “Invalid email or password.” and keeps the email value.
ActualResult: login-error visible with the documented message and the typed email preserved.

Scenario: The lockout state is explained to the user in the UI
Steps:
1. Submit the login form five times with a wrong password.
2. Look for the lockout banner.
ExpectedResult: The page shows the login-locked banner containing “locked” and refuses later attempts (including the correct password).
ActualResult: login-locked banner appears; the following correct-password attempt is still refused.

Scenario: Health endpoint reports service, database and seeded row count
Preconditions: App running against a seeded database.
Steps: 1. Call GET /api/health without a session.
ExpectedResult: 200 with status ok, service peoplecore-hrms, database ok, employees ≥ 10, seedDefects false.
ActualResult: 200 { status: ok, database: ok, employees: 10, seedDefects: false }.

Scenario: Error envelope for unknown routes without leaking internals
Steps: 1. Call an unmapped API path.
ExpectedResult: 404 with { error: { code: NOT_FOUND, message: … } }, no stack property, no data.
ActualResult: 404 NOT_FOUND, message echoes the requested path, no stack trace.

Scenario: Anonymous callers receive 401 and never data on every protected endpoint
Preconditions: No session cookie and no bearer token.
Steps: 1. Call each endpoint without credentials.
ExpectedResult: All five return 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and no data field.
ActualResult: All five endpoints returned 401 UNAUTHENTICATED with no data.

Scenario: Malformed JSON body and forged tokens are rejected
Steps:
1. POST /api/auth/login with broken JSON.
2. GET /api/auth/session with a forged bearer token.
ExpectedResult: 400 INVALID_JSON for the body and 401 for the forged token.
ActualResult: 400 INVALID_JSON and 401 respectively; a valid login afterwards still succeeds.

Scenario: Pagination contract: limit 1..100, 1-based pages, X-Total-Count
TestData: limit=100 (ok); limit=0, limit=101, limit=abc, page=0, page=-3 (rejected)
Steps:
1. Call /api/employees with the accepted value.
2. Call it with each rejected value.
ExpectedResult: limit=100 → 200; each invalid value → 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with details; every successful list carries X-Total-Count.
ActualResult: limit=100 accepted; 0/101/abc and page 0/-3 rejected with 400 and field details.

Scenario: Employee list search, department filter and empty state
Preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN, 10 seeded employees.
Steps:
1. Open /employees and note the row count.
2. Search for Okafor and apply.
3. Reset, filter by Engineering and apply.
4. Search for a non-existent name.
ExpectedResult: Search returns exactly the EMP-001 row; the department filter shows only Engineering rows; the empty search shows the empty-state block with a reset link.
ActualResult: 1 row for Okafor, 6 Engineering rows, empty-state visible for the unknown name (empty departmentId used to break the page — HR-BUG-006).
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-006.

Scenario: Sorting and pagination keep the active filters
Steps:
1. Call GET /api/employees?limit=5&sort=employeeCode&order=desc.
2. Request page=999.
3. On the page click Next and Previous.
ExpectedResult: Rows are sorted descending; page 1 has 5 rows; page 999 returns an empty array with the unchanged total; the page controls follow the filters.
ActualResult: Descending order confirmed; page 999 → data []; pagination-current shows 2 then 1 while limit=5 is preserved.

Scenario: Create an employee with a valid payload and verify the audit row
TestData: EMP-8xx, Probe Tester, probe.<stamp>@example.com, Probe#12345, EMPLOYEE, Engineering, 61000.5, 2023-06-01
Steps:

2. Read the Location header and the response body.

ExpectedResult: 201, Location /api/employees/<id>, email lower-cased, and exactly one EMPLOYEE_CREATE audit row with before null and after.salary present.
ActualResult: 201 with Location header, email normalised, one EMPLOYEE_CREATE audit row containing salary 76543.21.

Scenario: Duplicate employee code and duplicate email are conflicts
Preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN; one employee exists.
TestData: Same employee_code again; same email in UPPER case
Steps:
1. POST /api/employees with an existing code.
2. POST /api/employees with an existing email (different case).

Scenario: Boundary: salary range and decimal precision
Steps: 1. POST /api/employees for each value.
ExpectedResult: 422 INVALID_SALARY for out-of-range or 3-decimal values; 201 for the exact upper boundary and for two decimals.
Notes: The database also enforces CHECK (salary > 0 AND salary <= 1000000) — see DB-03/DB-04.

Scenario: Boundary: hire date window and calendar validity
Steps: 1. POST /api/employees for each date.
ExpectedResult: 422 INVALID_HIRE_DATE for the future and pre-1990 dates; 400 for the impossible calendar date; 201 for 1990-01-01.

Scenario: Delete an employee who owns attendance, leave and audit history
Preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN; the target submitted a leave request earlier.
TestData: employee with attendance row, PENDING leave request and LEAVE_CREATE audit row
Steps:
1. DELETE /api/employees/:id.
2. GET the record again.
3. Inspect the audit rows for the deleted id.
ExpectedResult: 204; the record is 404 afterwards; attendance/leave rows are gone; the LEAVE_CREATE audit row survives with actorId null (no 500).
ActualResult: After the fix: 204, child rows cascaded, audit row kept with actorId null (previously 500 — HR-BUG-008).
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-008; detected by the Postman cleanup folder.

Scenario: Deletion guards: self, manager with reports, unknown id
Steps: 1. DELETE each id.
ExpectedResult: 422 CANNOT_DELETE_SELF; 409 MANAGER_HAS_DIRECT_REPORTS; 404 for the unknown id.
ActualResult: 422 / 409 / 404 with the documented codes; the ADMIN account and the manager still exist.

Scenario: Partial update keeps untouched fields and audits before/after
Preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN; employee created by HR-TC-018.
TestData: PUT { firstName: "Renamed", salary: 52500.75, position: "Senior QA Engineer" }
Steps:
1. PUT the update.
2. Read the response.
3. GET /api/audit-logs?entityId=<id> and diff before/after.
ExpectedResult: 200 with the new values, unchanged email/code, and an EMPLOYEE_UPDATE row where before.salary = 50000 and after.salary = 52500.75.
ActualResult: Update applied, untouched fields preserved, audit diff shows 50000 → 52500.75.

Scenario: Type errors, unknown enums and unknown fields are 400
TestData: salary as string, role SUPERUSER, email not-an-email, password "password", extra field isSuperAdmin, departmentId 999, managerId 999, body { firstName: "Only" }
Steps: 1. POST each payload.
ExpectedResult: 400 with field details for the schema violations; 422 UNKNOWN_DEPARTMENT / UNKNOWN_MANAGER for the unknown references; the incomplete body lists every missing field.
ActualResult: All schema violations → 400 with details; unknown department/manager → 422 with specific codes; missing body reported 5+ fields.

Scenario: Employee code format boundaries
Steps: 1. POST /api/employees with each code.
ExpectedResult: All five return 400 with details[].path = employeeCode.
ActualResult: All five rejected with 400 and the employeeCode detail.
Notes: Valid shapes are EMP-### and EMP-#### (EMP-950 and EMP-9500 both pass).

Scenario: Unknown and non-numeric ids in the path
Steps: 1. Call each path.
ExpectedResult: 404 NOT_FOUND for the unknown id and 400 VALIDATION_ERROR for the non-numeric id.
ActualResult: 404 / 404 / 400 as documented.
Notes: In the browser the same paths render the 404 page — HR-TC-062.

Scenario: Combined filters are ANDed and q matches email and code as well as names
Steps:
1. Call the list endpoint with each filter set.
2. Verify every returned row matches all conditions.
ExpectedResult: One row for each exact query; every row of a combined filter satisfies both conditions; EMP-009/EMP-010 appear for the Sales+EMPLOYEE filter.
ActualResult: Filters combine correctly; 0 rows returned for the unknown search.

Scenario: Create an employee in the browser: inline validation first, then success
TestData: empty form; then EMP-7xx, Ursula Ito, ui.probe.<stamp>@example.com, Sales, 58500.50, UiProbe#12345
Steps:

3. Fill every field and submit.

Scenario: Edit an employee as HR: role and code are read-only
TestData: position “Backend Engineer III”, status ON_LEAVE, then restore
Steps:
1. Open /employees/4/edit.
2. Check the disabled controls.
3. Change position and status, save, verify the detail page, then restore the seeded values.
ExpectedResult: form-role and form-employeeCode are disabled with an explanation; the save is persisted and confirmed by the flash message; restoration returns the seeded state.
ActualResult: Disabled controls confirmed, update persisted, flash “Saved successfully.”, seeded values restored.

Scenario: Create a department, rename it and reject duplicates
TestData: Quality Engineering Qxx (created), rename, duplicate name "Engineering", duplicate code ENG
Steps:
1. POST /api/departments.
2. PUT the new id with a new name.
3. POST a duplicate name and a duplicate code.
ExpectedResult: 201 then 200; duplicates return 409 DUPLICATE_DEPARTMENT_NAME / DUPLICATE_DEPARTMENT_CODE; the audit trail holds DEPARTMENT_CREATE and DEPARTMENT_UPDATE.
ActualResult: 201/200/409/409 as expected and both audit rows present with different before/after names.

Scenario: Department write access is restricted to ADMIN/HR
Steps:
1. POST /api/departments as MANAGER.
2. PUT /api/departments/1 as EMPLOYEE.
3. GET /api/departments as EMPLOYEE.
ExpectedResult: Both writes return 403 while the read returns 200 — departments are readable by everyone but writable by ADMIN/HR only.
ActualResult: 403 / 403 / 200 as documented.

Scenario: Department validation: code shape and unknown ids
Steps:
1. POST the invalid pair.
2. PUT the unknown department.
ExpectedResult: 400 with details for both fields and 404 for the unknown id.
ActualResult: 400 (name + code details) and 404 recorded.

Scenario: Attendance list is scoped and filterable with a correct total
Preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN; 60 seeded rows.
TestData: limit=100; status=REMOTE; from>to; a range without data
Steps:
1. Call the list with each filter.
2. Compare X-Total-Count with the body total.
ExpectedResult: 60 seeded rows; only REMOTE rows for that filter; a swapped range returns 400; an empty range returns total 0 with an empty array.
ActualResult: X-Total-Count 60 on a fresh seed, REMOTE filter consistent, swapped range 400, empty range 0 rows.

Scenario: One row per employee per work date
Steps:
1. POST a valid attendance row.
2. POST the same employee/day again.
ExpectedResult: 201 then 409 DUPLICATE_ATTENDANCE.
ActualResult: 201 then 409 with the documented code; the database also enforces the UNIQUE index (DB-05).

Scenario: Time rules per status: LEAVE/ABSENT without times, PRESENT/REMOTE with times
TestData: checkIn 17:00 & checkOut 09:00; LEAVE with times; ABSENT with times; PRESENT without times; checkIn "9:00"
Steps: 1. POST each combination.
ExpectedResult: 422 INVALID_TIME_RANGE, 422 INVALID_ATTENDANCE_PAYLOAD (×3) and 400 for the malformed time format.
ActualResult: All invalid combinations rejected; ABSENT with times only failed after the fix (HR-BUG-002).
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-002.

Scenario: PATCH attendance writes an audit row and validates the merged state
Preconditions: Signed in as HR; one attendance row exists.
TestData: PATCH { status: REMOTE, checkOut: "18:00", notes: "…" }; PATCH with an empty body; PATCH an unknown id
Steps:
1. PATCH the row.
2. Check the audit trail.
3. PATCH with an empty body and with an unknown id.
ExpectedResult: 200 with the merged values, an ATTENDANCE_UPDATE audit row, 400 for the empty body and 404 for the unknown id.
ActualResult: 200 + ATTENDANCE_UPDATE audit row; empty body 400; unknown id 404.

Scenario: Terminated employees cannot receive attendance
Preconditions: Signed in as ADMIN; an employee was set to TERMINATED.
Steps: 1. Create an employee, set status TERMINATED, then POST attendance for them.
ExpectedResult: 422 EMPLOYEE_TERMINATED.
ActualResult: 422 EMPLOYEE_TERMINATED as documented.
Notes: Same rule for leave submission — HR-TC-050.

Scenario: Read-only employee view and scoped rows
Steps:
1. List own attendance.
2. Try to filter another employee.
3. Filter an empty date.
ExpectedResult: Only EMP-009 rows; 403 for the foreign employeeId; 0 rows for the empty date.
ActualResult: Own rows only, 403 for employeeId=4, and the UI shows the read-only notice without a create form.

Scenario: Record attendance in the browser and verify the filtered grid
TestData: first employee in the list, workDate today+50, REMOTE 08:45-17:15, notes “UI automation probe”
Steps:
1. Open /attendance and fill the record form.
2. Submit and read the flash message.
3. Filter from/to = that date with status REMOTE.
ExpectedResult: Flash “Created successfully.”, exactly one matching row with 08:45 and REMOTE, and the total count reflects the filter.
ActualResult: Flash shown, the filtered grid returned one REMOTE row with the entered times.

Scenario: Submit leave and verify the computed inclusive day count
Steps:
1. POST /api/leave-requests.
2. Read the response.
3. GET the audit trail for the new id.
ExpectedResult: 201 with days = 3, status PENDING, reviewedBy null and a LEAVE_CREATE audit row.
ActualResult: 201, days 3 (inclusive), PENDING, LEAVE_CREATE audit row with after.days = 3.

Scenario: Reason length boundaries 9/10 and 500/501 characters
TestData: reason of 9 chars (rejected), 10 chars (accepted); 501 chars (rejected), 500 chars (accepted)
Steps: 1. POST each variant with non-overlapping date windows.
ExpectedResult: 400 with details[].path = reason for 9 and 501 characters; 201 for 10 and 500.
ActualResult: 9 chars → 400; 501 chars → 400; the accepted boundaries were verified with the 30-day case.

Scenario: Date order and calendar validity
Steps: 1. POST each variant.
ExpectedResult: 422 INVALID_LEAVE_RANGE for the reversed range and 400 for the impossible calendar date.
ActualResult: 422 INVALID_LEAVE_RANGE and 400 respectively.

Scenario: Maximum request length: 30 days accepted, 31 days rejected
TestData: today+200 → today+229 (30 days); today+100 → today+130 (31 days)
Steps:
1. POST the 31-day request.
2. POST the 30-day request.
ExpectedResult: 422 LEAVE_TOO_LONG for 31 days and 201 with days = 30 for the boundary case.
ActualResult: 31 days → 422 LEAVE_TOO_LONG; 30 days → 201 with days 30.

Scenario: Overlap detection against PENDING and APPROVED requests plus the adjacent-date boundary
Preconditions: employee6 owns the seeded PENDING request (today+10 → today+12); employee2 owns an APPROVED request (today-12 → today-11).
TestData: exact window; today+11→+13; single day today+12; adjacent today+13→+14; -11→-10 against the approved request
Steps: 1. POST each variant.
ExpectedResult: 409 LEAVE_OVERLAP for every intersecting window; 201 for the adjacent request; 409 against the APPROVED request.
ActualResult: All overlapping variants → 409; adjacent dates → 201; the SQL detection query was separately verified in DB-08.
Notes: With SEED_DEFECTS=1 the same-day variant is accepted — see HR-SEEDED-02.

Scenario: Manager approves a direct report request and further transitions are refused
Preconditions: employee6 submitted a PENDING request; signed in as manager (EMP-003).
Steps:
1. Approve the request.
2. Approve again.
3. Try to reject it.
ExpectedResult: 200 with APPROVED, reviewer Sofia Marchetti and the comment; 422 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION for both later attempts.
ActualResult: Approval stored with reviewer and comment; the second approve and the reject both returned 422.

Scenario: Rejection requires a comment of at least 5 characters
Preconditions: employee6 submitted a PENDING request; signed in as manager.
TestData: {} (missing), { comment: "no" } (too short), { comment: "Team is at capacity." } (valid)
Steps:
1. Reject without a comment.
2. Reject with 2 characters.
3. Reject with a valid comment.
ExpectedResult: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR for the first two and 200 REJECTED with the stored comment for the third.
ActualResult: 400 / 400 / 200 with reviewComment persisted and reviewedAt set.

Scenario: Cancel own PENDING request; reviewed or foreign requests cannot be cancelled
TestData: own PENDING request; the same request again; an APPROVED request of another employee; a PENDING request of another employee
Steps:
1. DELETE the own PENDING request.
2. DELETE it again.
3. DELETE request 2 (APPROVED, EMP-005).
4. DELETE request 6 (PENDING, EMP-010).
ExpectedResult: 200 CANCELLED, then 422 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION, 403 and 403.
ActualResult: 200 CANCELLED followed by 422/403/403 with the documented codes.
Notes: An APPROVED request owned by the caller also returns 422 (see the Postman flow).

Scenario: Nobody may review their own request

2. PATCH /api/leave-requests/:id/approve as the same user.
ExpectedResult: 201 for the submission and 403 when reviewing it; the owner can still cancel it.
ActualResult: 403 on the self-review, 200 on the cancellation.

Scenario: Terminated employees cannot submit or receive a leave decision
Preconditions: A newly created employee with manager 3; a stale session obtained before termination.

Steps:
1. Submit a request as the employee.
2. Set the employee to TERMINATED as ADMIN.
3. Submit again with the stale session.
4. Approve the old request as the manager.
ExpectedResult: 201 for the submission while ACTIVE; afterwards the stale session is revoked (401 UNAUTHENTICATED) and the pending request can no longer be approved (422 EMPLOYEE_TERMINATED).
ActualResult: 201 while active; after termination the stale cookie returned 401 (session revoked — HR-BUG-012) and the manager review returned 422 EMPLOYEE_TERMINATED.
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-012.

Scenario: Employee submits and cancels leave through the browser
TestData: today+80 → today+82; reason “short” first, then a 56-character reason
Steps:

2. Read the inline error and correct the reason.
3. Submit and find the new row.
4. Cancel it.

ActualResult: Whole journey verified in one browser session including the state change after cancelling.

Scenario: Manager review queue: short comment rejected, then approve/reject

TestData: rejection comment “no” (too short), then “Team is at capacity that week.”
Steps:

2. Reject with 2 characters.

4. Approve the next request.

Scenario: Leave list scoping, pagination and status filter

Steps:

Scenario: Audit trail content, filtering and salary visibility
Steps:

2. Filter by entity.
3. Inspect the seeded EMPLOYEE_CREATE payload.
4. Filter an id without history.
ExpectedResult: Parsed rows with actorEmail and JSON before/after; salary present in the payload; exactly one row per entity filter; an empty array with total 0 for the unknown id.

Scenario: Audit page shows the diff for a specific employee
Steps:

Scenario: Summary report content and scope

Scenario: Postman end-to-end flow (login → employee → attendance → leave → RBAC → audit → cleanup)

Scenario: Seeding is deterministic and the schema enforces the documented rules

Scenario: Direct API access matrix for all four roles

Scenario: A rejected browser journey is explained with a real 403 page

Scenario: Responsive layout at 1440x900 and 390x844
Preconditions: Screenshots captured from the running app.
Steps:
1. Capture the desktop and mobile viewports.
2. Inspect the responsive breakpoints, the skip link and the table layout.
ExpectedResult: Both viewports render usable layouts: navigation wraps, tables remain readable (less important columns hidden below 620px), the skip link is present and the mobile dashboard/list stay usable.

Scenario: Attendance write authorization across all four roles
Preconditions: Sessions for EMPLOYEE (employee1), MANAGER and ADMIN.
TestData: POST /api/attendance for a direct report, for an unrelated employee and as EMPLOYEE
Steps:
1. As EMPLOYEE: POST attendance for own id.
2. As MANAGER: POST attendance for a direct report (EMP-004).
3. As MANAGER: POST attendance for EMP-001 (outside the team).
ExpectedResult: 403 for the employee, 201 (or 409 if the day is taken) for the direct report and 403 for the out-of-scope employee — never a successful write outside the caller scope.
ActualResult: 403 / 201 / 403 as documented; this case failed before the fix with 201 for the employee (HR-BUG-004).
Notes: Regression case for HR-BUG-004 — the critical privilege escalation found in this project.

Scenario: HR never sees destructive controls and cannot change a role in the browser
Preconditions: Signed in as HR; signed in as ADMIN in a second context.
Steps:
1. Open the employee detail as HR.
2. Check for a delete control.
3. Open the edit form and inspect the role/code controls.
4. Try to edit the ADMIN account.
ExpectedResult: No delete button and no create link for HR; role and employee code are disabled with an explanation; editing an ADMIN account renders the 403 page; ADMIN does see the delete button and enabled controls.
ActualResult: HR: no delete control, disabled role/code, 403 for the ADMIN record; ADMIN: delete + enabled controls + audit nav.

Scenario: Keyboard-only navigation and visible focus indicators
Preconditions: App running in a browser (planned manual session).
TestData: Tab through /login, /employees and /leave without a mouse.
Steps:
1. Press Tab from the address bar and follow the focus order.
2. Verify every interactive control can be reached and activated with Enter/Space.
3. Check that the focus ring is visible at every step.
ExpectedResult: Logical focus order that starts at the skip link, all controls reachable, a visible focus outline (3px #2563eb) on every focused element.
Notes: Manual keyboard session not performed in this run. The automation only asserts that the skip link, labels and semantic headings exist (see HR-TC-063); a full keyboard pass is listed under Known limitations in the README.

Scenario: Colour contrast of status badges, alerts and links (WCAG AA)
Preconditions: App running in a browser (planned manual session).
TestData: Status badges (ACTIVE/ON_LEAVE/TERMINATED), alert boxes, table headers.
Steps:
1. Measure the contrast of each badge/alert foreground/background pair.
2. Compare with the WCAG AA 4.5:1 (normal text) / 3:1 (large text) thresholds.
ExpectedResult: Every text/background pair reaches at least the AA threshold; otherwise the colour pair is documented as a defect.
Notes: No contrast checker is installed — the dependency set is fixed by the portfolio standard (express/ejs/zod + chosen dev tooling), so axe/pa11y could not be added. Documented as a limitation instead of being claimed.

Scenario: Screen-reader pass over the leave review flow
Preconditions: A screen reader (NVDA) available; app running.
TestData: The manager review queue and the leave form.
Steps:
1. Navigate the leave page with the screen reader.
2. Verify that form labels, error messages and flash messages are announced.
ExpectedResult: Every control has an announced label, errors are associated with their field and the flash message is announced as a status region.
Notes: No screen-reader session was performed; the markup already uses role="status"/role="alert" and explicit labels, which is verified structurally by HR-TC-051.

Scenario: Cross-browser smoke test (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)
TestData: npm run test:ui with the Firefox and WebKit projects.
Steps:
1. Run the UI suite with each browser engine.
2. Compare the results.
ExpectedResult: The suite passes on all three engines.
